### Renamed to MuxSU, and set up again after updating

**DisplayMuxAuto is now MuxSU.** The name, the icons and the app identifier have all changed.

**After updating, every computer needs setting up again**: shared displays, input ports,
paired hosts, the pairing password, language and theme are not carried over. A new
identifier makes this a new app as far as the system is concerned, and it cannot read what
the old one saved.

- **Windows**: the installer removes an old DisplayMux or DisplayMuxAuto install and its
  autostart entry before installing MuxSU, so two copies are never left starting at login.
- **macOS**: the menu bar item and its Open/Quit menu use the new name.

### Update every computer together

**v0.4.0 cannot pair with v0.3.0 or earlier.** Update every computer that takes part in
switching at the same time.

- Local network discovery now advertises `_muxsu._tcp` instead of `_displaymux._tcp`, so old
  and new versions cannot see each other.
- The agent protocol moves from 2 to 3. A reply from a different version is rejected, with a
  prompt to update that host.

### Safer pairing

- **The pairing password must now be at least 15 characters** (previously 8).
- The password is no longer used as the key directly: the network authentication key is
  derived from it with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations.
- The complete agent reply, including its protocol version, is signed. A client uses nothing
  from a reply until it has verified the signature and an exact protocol-version match.

This closes the two known limitations carried since v0.2.0: unauthenticated reply contents,
and a password used with no KDF.

### New look

- A new app icon and menu bar glyph.
- The interface takes on a translucent, glass-like treatment in the manner of macOS.

### Why the version jumps to 0.4.0

By `docs/versioning.md`: updating asks the user to set things up again (rule 1), a host on
the previous version can no longer pair with an updated one (rule 2), and the app's name has
changed (rule 3). All three apply.

### Known limitations

- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper
  may require manual approval.
